## 4. Mission Deep-Dives

### MISSION-027: Forensic MLX Server Lifecycle Hardening: Process Group Teardown, Port Listen Scoping, and Scheduled Idle Reaping (Rank #1)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `CORROBORATED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: macOS / Apple Silicon MLX Process & Memory Management
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit` (Tier: `free-local`, CLI: `mlx-lm`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Refactoring mlx_server_manager.py to: (1) scope port discovery via `lsof -ti -sTCP:LISTEN :<port>`, (2) terminate the complete process group (`os.killpg`) to guarantee child Python model termination, (3) measure true Metal unified memory RSS from the listening worker child, and (4) hook idle reaping to Protocol 128 session timers will guarantee 100% memory reclamation (~4.7 GiB) and eliminate zombie daemon leaks.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > After executing `stop_server`, any child python process remains listening on :8080, memory RSS fails to reflect the model weight allocation, or client TCP sockets are returned by port discovery.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-03T15:58:53.700072+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-027/README.md): Pre-registered. RED on the old code: 4/4 defects reproduced with a stub launcher->worker tree (discovery returned a client PID; stop left the worker listening; stop reported 'stopped' while a worker ignoring SIGTERM survived; status reported the launcher). After the fix: 20/20 stub cycles and 8/8 real-model cycles (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-4bit on spare port 8099; :8080 untouched) with verified teardown, 0 survivors, 0 client PIDs; safety rule holds (process groups containing non-MLX processes fall back to a tree kill; stale state PIDs are never signalled). Real-model footprint 4,304-4,361 MB warm; system free memory recovered about 24% -> 52% after stop. Idle reaping limited to managed servers and hooked into the Protocol 128 boot (guardian_wakeup) and closure steps. Pre-registered misses: fresh-boot footprint was 562-3,317 MB (>=4,000 predicted) and ps RSS was not <100 MB for fresh servers; the warm measurement point was added after the miss and labelled as an amendment.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * The mission's literal lsof command (lsof -ti -sTCP:LISTEN :PORT) is invalid on macOS; use lsof -nP -iTCP:PORT -sTCP:LISTEN -t. Plain lsof -ti :PORT also returns client sockets.
  * ps RSS is not a usable memory measure for MLX (10 MB for a 4.7 GB worker on a long-lived server because the pages are compressed; 0.3-2 GB on fresh ones); use footprint -p PID on the listening worker, and measure after a warm-up generation because the model loads lazily (fresh 0.5-3.3 GB, warm about 4.3 GB).
  * A stop check that compares the listener PID with the launcher PID reports success while the worker survives; verify by checking nothing listens on the port and no tracked process is alive.
  * Signal a process group only when every member is an MLX process; otherwise tree-kill the worker and launcher. Never signal a state-file PID that no longer looks like an MLX process.
  * Reaping must be limited to servers the manager started; a hand-launched persistent daemon is never reaped. Pre-register thresholds with the measurement point (fresh vs warm) stated, or the first live run can miss for a reason that is about measurement, not the code.

### MISSION-031: Automated Blast-Radius & Projected Impact Analysis for Multi-Agent Worktree Concurrency (Rank #4)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `CORROBORATED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: macOS / Python 3.11+ / Git Worktrees & Coordination Flight Board
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit` (Tier: `free-local`, CLI: `mlx-lm`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Augmenting mission manifests with native 'projected_impact' declarations and extending manage_coordination.py with an automated overlap matrix enables the flight board to automatically acquire exact target leases, surface disjoint parallel dispatches to incoming agents, and eliminate 100% of concurrent worktree merge conflicts without manual target path configuration.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > An agent is able to check out a mission that silently conflicts with an active lease, manual --targets are still required at CLI checkout for registered missions, or collision detection overhead exceeds 500ms.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-04T06:39:43.017569+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-031/README.md): Pre-registered. Old flow (no --targets, loaded from git at c48db6b6a): 284 of 284 genuinely overlapping random mission pairs checked out silently (100% silent conflicts); 3/3 RED tests failed. New flow (projected_impact in the manifest, conservative component-wise overlap, shared generated files excluded): 500 pairs, 0 false negatives, 284/284 overlaps blocked, 0 manual --targets needed, 15 false positives (6.9%). Latency: registry matrix+dispatch p95 5.6 ms; per-mission lease check p95 0.19 ms at 200 missions/20 leases; 200-mission matrix 175 ms. Real git, 60 branch pairs: 0 conflicts among 23 predicted-disjoint pairs; 0 unpredicted conflicts; verify flagged 20/20 planted undeclared edits with 0 false alarms. Live registry: suggest returns 3 mutually disjoint missions (031, 023, 030); 13 open missions can run in parallel. Boundary: index.jsonl conflicted in 60/60 merges (regenerated by every mission): flagged as regenerate_after_merge, not eliminated. Dogfooding verify: 1 of 33 files of this mission was outside its own declaration (test_relay.py, also declared by MISSION-032). Shipped: impact.py, manifest-driven checkout, matrix/suggest/verify, relay dispatchable line, manage_backlog validation, 20 backfilled declarations, 36 new tests.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * A lease with no locks can never conflict: manifest-declared impact (projected_impact) makes checkout lock exactly what a mission touches, and refusing an undeclared lock-free checkout closes the silent under-locking hole.
  * Conservative overlap with a leaf rule (a path with an extension has no children) gave 0 false negatives at a 6.9% false-positive rate; two wildcard components are assumed to match, a cheap head/tail refinement would cut the false positives further.
  * Declarations are only as good as verify: run manage_coordination.py verify before the PR; a mission's own manifest and shared generated files are implicitly allowed, everything else outside the declaration breaks the no-conflict guarantee.
  * The hypothesis claim of eliminating 100% of merge conflicts does not hold for files every mission regenerates (index.jsonl conflicted in 60/60 merges); they need regeneration at merge time (MISSION-034), not locks.
  * Fix the checkout side effect at its root: write the IN_PROGRESS marker into the new worktree's manifest copy, not the main tree. Matrix performance: normalise once per mission (1.29 s -> 0.2 s at 200 missions).

- **Falsification Gate**:
  > A successor agent from a different vendor contradicts an established architectural invariant, repeats a previously verified benchmark without citation, or requires human intervention to discover the preceding model's work.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-04T06:14:17.223817+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-025/README.md): Pre-registered A/B on 22 questions (14 from real ledgers, 8 from a synthetic Codex->Gemini->Claude handover chain), local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B as the incoming agent, temperature 0, same loop and tools in both conditions. Control (briefing without relay): 5/22 = 22.7% correct, median 5 turns, 2.5 tool calls per question. Treatment (Predecessor Relay in the briefing): 15/22 = 68.2% (+45.5 points), median 2 turns, 1.27 tool calls, 14.6 s vs 31.1 s per question. Pre-registered bar (>= 90% correct, zero tool calls on >= 90% of questions, no contradicting answers) not met, and the decision rule (treatment < 80% -> FALSIFIED) applies. All 7 treatment misses had the answer present in the relay: the agent ignored the briefing and dug with tools (4), copied a format placeholder (1), confused ids in one note (2). Relay size held (20 lines, 1,957 characters live; 3,245 worst case). Feature shipped: relay.py, guardian_wakeup integration, manage_coordination checkin --handoff, docs, 26 tests. Limits: one weak incoming agent, n=22, single run; frontier successors and handoff adoption untested.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Surfacing a predecessor relay in the boot briefing triples a 7B incoming agent's correctness and halves its discovery work, but does not by itself reach 90%: the weak agent often ignores the briefing and digs with tools; the answers were present every time.
  * Measure the incoming agent's tool-call syntax before attributing control failures to missing information: a control run failed four turns in a row on <search_text>query</search_text>, a parse artifact that would have inflated the relay's value; the shared loop now accepts that form.
  * A handoff note states the next step last, so a short display cap hides the most important part; show recent notes up to two thirds of the storage cap and keep the whole section under a fixed budget.
  * Only 2 of 10 resolved missions cite a file path as evidence; the relay falls back to the experiment log or the mission manifest. Record-result callers should pass --citation with a path.
  * Format placeholders in a question (VERDICT | path) can be copied literally by a small model; use a worked example or JSON in the answer format. Test frontier incoming agents and relay-first placement next (MISSION-032).

- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-03T14:43:53.074952+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-022/README.md): Frozen local_agent_loop.py on Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-4bit/MLX, 30 generated held-out tasks per run, exact-match grading, temp 0, max 5 turns. - **Falsification Gate**:

LIMIT: cold process with warm OS page cache, one machine and model, 2 s test threshold, 1-token requests.

### MISSION-063: Braess's Paradox for Random Walks in Trees: Does Adding a Shortcut Edge Increase Kemeny's Constant, and Is the Paradox Concentrated at Distance 2? (Rank #36)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: Spectral graph theory and finite Markov chains: Kemeny's constant under single-edge additions across all non-isomorphic trees on n = 4..11 vertices (exact enumeration in zero-dependency Python standard library; bounded local CPU)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `gemini-3.8-flash` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `agy`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Let Delta_K(T, e) = K(T + e) - K(T) be the change in Kemeny's constant when adding a single missing edge e = {u, v} at tree distance d_T(u, v) >= 2 to a tree T on n vertices. Across all non-isomorphic free trees on each held-out vertex count n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11}: (H1, Prevalence & Growth) At least 5% of all missing-edge additions (T, e) at each n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11} exhibit Braess's paradox (Delta_K(T, e) > 10^-9), and the paradox fraction p(n) increases strictly monotonically across n = 7, 8, 9, 10, 11. (H2, Distance-2 Triangle-Trap Concentration vs Diameter Shortcuts) Across all held-out Braess-paradox pairs (T, e) on n in {7..11}, at least 80% occur at tree distance d_T(u, v) = 2 (forming a local 3-cycle), whereas zero diameter-endpoint shortcuts (d_T(u, v) = diam(T)) ever increase Kemeny's constant (max over diameter shortcuts of Delta_K(T, e) < -10^-9). (H3, Instrument Validity Gate) Free-tree counts match OEIS A000055 (2, 3, 6, 11, 23, 47, 106, 235 for n = 4..11) with zero isomorphic duplicates; fundamental-matrix hitting-time K_hit(G) is invariant across all starting vertices within 10^-11 and agrees with the spectral formula K_spec(G) = sum_{k=2}^n 1/(1 - lambda_k(P)) within 10^-11 on every evaluated graph; and closed-form identities hold for K_n ((n-1)^2/n) and C_n ((n^2-1)/6).
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > The hypothesis is FALSIFIED if either H1 (paradox prevalence >= 5% at every n in {7..11} and strict monotonicity p(7) < p(8) < p(9) < p(10) < p(11)) or H2 (>= 80% of paradoxes at distance d_T(u, v) = 2 and zero paradoxes at d_T(u, v) = diam(T)) fails on the held-out domain n in {7, 8, 9, 10, 11} given a passing validity gate H3. If any check in H3 fails or the computation does not complete the held-out domain within budget, the mission is UNASSESSED (never FALSIFIED or CORROBORATED). Development trees (n in {4, 5, 6}) are used strictly for instrument verification before freezing; protocol.md, freeze.json and the evaluator script are committed and hash-frozen before any held-out n in {7..11} is evaluated. Secondary breakdowns (by shortcut distance, automorphism-orbit deduplication, or unweighted mean first passage time) are descriptive only and cannot rescue a failed primary claim.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-08T15:06:44.642192+00:00` [antigravity] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-063/README.md): H3 passed (OEIS A000055 exact on n=4..11; Gauss-Jordan vs Jacobi spectral max diff 2.77e-13 across 16,355 held-out pairs; freeze commit d584005b2 preceded held-out commit ccb41f431). H1a held (paradox rate 20.00%, 18.22%, 15.50%, 14.49%, 13.83% >= 5% on n=7..11; 2340/16355 = 14.31% overall) and H2a held (87.65% of held-out paradoxes at distance d=2, 11.75% at d=3, 0.60% at d=4, 0% at d>=5). Falsified on H1b (raw paradox fraction decreases monotonically with n from 20.00% to 13.83%, while orbit-deduplicated fraction stays nearly flat at 11.39%-13.30% and max Delta_K increases from +1.2619 to +3.4939) and H2b (145/1746 diameter-endpoint shortcuts increase K(T), with max Delta_K = +0.439394; since 0 paradoxes occur at any shortcut distance d>=5, all 145 occur in trees with diam<=4).
  * `2026-11-08T15:20:13+00:00` [claude-opus-5-5] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-063/independent-review-opus.md): Independent adversarial review via cli-agent (--cli claude --model claude-opus-5-5 --effort low --isolated --clean-context, 97.02s) confirmed the FALSIFIED verdict (H1b and H2b fail, H3 and core numerics hold) and surfaced 11 documentation/caveat fixes (R1-R4, J1-J5, L1-L3, M1-M5, E1-E3, V1-V2), all incorporated into README.md and MISSION-063.json while keeping frozen artifacts untouched.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * For n in {7..11}, all 2,340 observed random-walk Braess paradoxes in trees occurred at shortcut distances d_T(u,v) in {2, 3, 4} (87.65% at d=2, 11.75% at d=3, 0.60% at d=4, and 0 at d>=5), with the d=2 share declining from 100.00% at n=7 to 85.50% at n=11; whether d>=5 paradoxes emerge at n>=12 remains open.
  * Across n in {7..11}, the raw missing-edge paradox fraction p(n) fell monotonically (20.00% to 13.83%) even as the maximum slowdown Delta_K rose (+1.2619 to +3.4939), whereas the automorphism-orbit-deduplicated paradox fraction stayed nearly flat (11.39% to 13.30%), showing that raw edge-pair prevalence is sensitive to automorphism multiplicity.
  * Diameter-endpoint shortcuts are not immune to Braess's paradox when the tree diameter itself is small (145/1,746 diameter shortcuts increased K(T), all at diam(T) <= 4); for n <= 11, no shortcut at distance d_T(u,v) >= 5 increased K(T).
  * When dispatching Claude CLI for isolated read-only reviews via cli-agent, always pass --clean-context (which sets a neutral cwd, --setting-sources project, --disable-slash-commands, and --tools '') so repository hooks and tool initialization do not cause timeouts.

### MISSION-057: Do consecutive primes remember their last digit beyond what a random model predicts, and does that memory fade as the primes grow? (Rank #37)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: Number theory: last-digit transitions between consecutive primes (exact sieve to 10^8, bounded local CPU)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `claude`)
- **Fallback Models**: `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Let P(d->d) be the probability that the next prime has the same last digit d in {1,3,7,9}, and let C(d->d) be the same quantity in a Cramer-style random control (each integer coprime to 10 included independently with probability 2.5/ln n, which itself gives a value below 0.25 at finite size). Repulsion R_d = C(d->d) - P(d->d). (H1) In the primes within [10^7, 10^8], R_d >= 0.5 percentage points for EVERY digit d. (H2) For every digit d, R_d is larger in [10^5, 10^6] than in [10^7, 10^8]. (H3, instrument validity) The simulated control matches its analytic value q(1-q)^3/(1-(1-q)^4) within 0.3 percentage points for every digit in both windows.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > FALSIFIED if H1 or H2 fails for any digit given a valid control. If H3 fails or any instrument check fails the result is UNASSESSED. Thresholds, windows, control definition and aggregation are fixed in protocol.md before the held-out run and not changed afterwards. Secondary tables cannot rescue a failed primary claim. REVISION NOTE: the first draft compared primes with the naive independence value 0.25; the development run showed the random control itself sits near 0.16 at these sizes (waiting-time geometry), so 0.25 is the wrong null and the comparison was redefined to the control BEFORE the held-out run; this is disclosed in protocol.md.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-06T17:57:51.866564+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-057/README.md): H1 held (real primes repel own last digit beyond the Cramer control by 1.8/2.8/2.8/1.8 pp for digits 1/3/7/9 at 10^7-10^8). H2 failed: the extra repulsion did not fade between 10^5-10^6 and 10^7-10^8 (digit 1 +0.65 pp, digit 9 +0.44 pp, digits 3/7 within noise). H3 instrument validity held (control matches analytic formula within 0.3 pp). Random control gives ~0.16-0.20, not 0.25; baseline redefined before the held-out run.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * The naive 25% null is wrong for primes of finite size: a Cramer random model already gives 16-20% for same-digit returns because of geometric waiting; compare against the model, not the naive value.
  * The repulsion beyond the random model is persistent (not fading) across two decades; the fading part is the random-model-explained part.

### MISSION-041: Compile Falsification Criteria into Executable Property Tests and Counterexample Searches (Rank #38)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: Local Python hypothesis/property testing harness; evaluating-agent-work; deterministic execution (ceiling 500k tokens, 6 CPU-hours)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `cli-agent`)
- **Fallback Models**: `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > For bounded Python components, an agent that translates preregistered claims into property tests and counterexample searches will: (a) detect >= 80% of held-out, non-equivalent semantic mutants; (b) improve detection by >= 20 percentage points over equal-budget example-test generation; (c) produce <= 5% false alarms against verified reference implementations; and (d) finish within 10 minutes per component, excluding initial environment setup.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > Any threshold missed falsifies the hypothesis. Tests that merely reproduce the implementation behavior without an independent specification do not count. A timeout is not proof of correctness.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-06T05:28:57.083147+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-041/v3/results.md @41f2a57b5): v3 frozen-before-scoring benchmark, 20 components, 80 held-out non-equivalent source-level mutants: property 66.25% (needs >=80%), example 78.75% (gain -12.5pp, needs +20pp), existing 68.75%, 0/20 false alarms, max 1.2s computation-only. Independently reviewed (Claude reviewer of Codex work, accepted conditionally). Scope: full-oracle property arm, procedural holdout, 20 clusters of 4; no-oracle property arm untested. v1 pilot and v2 (invalid, errata) retained, not pooled.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Equal-budget example sampling over small exhaustive domains saturates; a benchmark must show per-mutant kill density before the arms are compared.
  * Redundant relations alongside a full oracle do not test metamorphic properties.
  * Commit the freeze to git before scoring.

### MISSION-050: Adaptive Progress Checkpointing Optimized for Interruption Risk and Verified Recovery (Rank #42)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `hybrid`
- **Target Platform**: Multi-agent coordination harness; manage_coordination.py; relay.py; evaluating-agent-work telemetry (ceiling 1M tokens, 12 execution-hours)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `cli-agent`)
- **Fallback Models**: `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > A checkpoint policy using measured interruption risk, progress value, and checkpoint cost will: (a) produce >= 20% more verified completed subgoals per fixed resource budget than the best fixed-interval policy on development data; (b) lose <= 5% of acknowledged progress; (c) keep checkpoint overhead <= 10% of inference tokens; and (d) lose no more than 3% throughput in interruption-free controls.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > Fail if any threshold is missed, or if the adaptive policy uses advance knowledge of the held-out interruption schedule.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-06T07:10:54.800563+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-050/v2/results.md + orchestrator-addendum.md): Frozen v2 candidate (cold-start repair with pre-registered prior), all 630 planned trials complete (simulation 1,620 trials; real-agent arm with local Qwen: 30 tasks x 7 policies x development/held-out/control). Simulation: gain -14.9% dev / -11.6% held-out (needs >=20%), acknowledged loss 47.7% / 46.2% (needs <=5%), control throughput loss 3.5998% (needs <=3%). Real arm: gain -78.0% dev / -71.7% held-out, loss 93.2% / 90.9%, checkpoint overhead 7.6-8.0% (pass), control loss 0.0% frozen measure and 1.09% by request service time (pass by construction: adaptive behaved as end-only, 0 early requests in 90 trials). Independent reviews (Claude reviewer of Codex work): simulation accepted; real arm changes-requested then fixed (adaptive == end-only by arithmetic; budget infeasible: even the best fixed policy loses 57-58%; 1,113/1,282 wrong calls were identical deterministic repeats; ~46% of budget unused; v2 prior chosen post hoc after v1 held-out). Scope: this frozen design and candidate, not adaptive checkpointing in general; handoff and quota denial simulated; real arm tested a sequential request driver, not a live long-context agent. Contention: 58% of summed wall time was lock wait; metrics are token-based; control claim re-checked on service time; one interrupted trial preserved and rerun, reproduced exactly.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * A policy whose trigger cannot fire inside the trial budget degenerates to the baseline; check feasibility before a real-agent run.
  * Interrupted trials: preserve the partial snapshot, rerun deterministically, exclude by explicit response id, assert reproduction.
  * A shared model lock held by the orchestrator can stall a worker that misreads the wait as a timeout.

### MISSION-054: Make Evaluation Earn Its Cost: Close the Loop from Observed Failures to Verified Procedural Repairs and Measured Savings (Rank #43)
- **Status**: `IN_PROGRESS`
- **Execution Surface**: `hybrid`
- **Target Platform**: evaluating-agent-work skill (sanctuary-core); existing scoring, usage telemetry, procedure-outcome and memory mechanisms; deterministic Python/shell checks; proposed additional inference ceiling 150k total tokens (an initial ceiling, not a target)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `claude`)
- **Fallback Models**: `gpt-6-luna`, `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > A minimal extension to the existing evaluation workflow can convert evidenced recurring failures into small verified repairs while reducing repeated operational waste. Purpose: evaluation should produce better subsequent execution within a limited subscription budget (perform useful work, identify an evidenced recurring failure, select a proportionate repair, verify it cheaply, apply it during later real work, measure whether it helped). Scores, dashboards, documents and extra research missions are supporting artifacts, not the objective; recognition, resource budgets and authorization stay separate and evaluation results never grant permissions. CLAIM A (proportionate decisions and enforceable checks): across 12 frozen, held-out operational scenarios the revised workflow selects the preregistered appropriate evaluation/repair action in >= 10 of 12 cases, passes every designated critical invariant, produces no change outside the scenario's authorization or declared scope, and uses deterministic verification wherever it adequately tests the claim. Critical invariants: (1) never declare an unfinished outcome complete; (2) never expand authorization because of a high score; (3) never silently weaken required experiments to fit a budget; (4) never represent missing telemetry as zero cost or zero interventions; (5) never present artifact hashes as proof of behavioral correctness. The unrevised baseline is reported too; if it already performs well no gain is manufactured. CLAIM B (measured operational value): across the next 12 eligible real work units collected during already-authorized missions: (i) the recurrence rate of the specifically targeted failures falls by >= 30% relative to a frozen, comparable historical baseline (denominator = applicable opportunities, not all tasks; counts reported with rates); (ii) total measured evaluation overhead is <= 15% of total measured model-token consumption across those units; (iii) accepted-outcome completion rate falls by <= 5 percentage points relative to the comparable baseline; (iv) no acceptance criteria or scientific requirements are weakened to achieve savings. Historical comparison is observational, not a randomized causal demonstration.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > Claim A is falsified if its scenario threshold or any critical invariant fails in a valid completed evaluation. Claim B is falsified if its thresholds fail in a valid, sufficiently comparable completed observation window. If there are too few relevant failure opportunities, missing usage measurements, or no defensible historical baseline, Claim B is UNASSESSED and the reason is stated; absence of evidence is neither success nor failure. Minimum usable denominators are specified before collection and not revised after seeing outcomes; no artificial work is launched to increase the sample. Claims are reported separately: no overall CORROBORATED verdict while a required claim is unassessed. If the evidence-contract and status capabilities cannot express partial assessment, the mission stays open and the limitation is recorded. If the intervention adds overhead without sufficient benefit it is simplified or removed and the finding preserved.

### MISSION-051: Usage Prediction That Works at Small N: Size Buckets, Resolvable Window Readings and a Same-Bucket Cross-Model Effort Ratio (Rank #44)

  > If agents declare one of three size buckets (small, medium, large) at checkout instead of a free-text task class, and the percent-to-token calibration is fitted only on measurements where the window moved by at least 3 percentage points (or on tasks pooled to that size), then once 40 measured tasks exist with at least 8 per bucket: (a) the held-out token MAPE of the per-bucket median predictor is at most 30% and at least 20% below the static per-task ceilings; (b) the calibrated percent-to-token estimate lands within +/-50% on at least 8 of 10 held-out measurements; and (c) for at least one bucket run on two models, the measured effort ratio (wall time, cost, retries) differs from 1.0 by more than the run-to-run spread of the cheaper model.
- **Falsification Gate**:

### MISSION-058: Discover and investigate an unfamiliar question through Moltbook, preserving a reproducible successor handoff (Rank #45)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `hybrid`
- **Target Platform**: Agent intellectual exploration, research discovery and persistent learning (public Moltbook read-only access, bounded web research, local computation)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `claude`)
- **Fallback Models**: `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Within the fixed discovery and investigation budget, public Moltbook material yields at least one question new to the inspected Sanctuary knowledge base that is investigated using evidence beyond Moltbook, produces at least one substantiated finding or resolved uncertainty, and supports a fresh successor session correctly answering at least 4 of 5 frozen handoff questions from preserved artifacts.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > FALSIFIED if any of: (1) A completed valid discovery pass yields no candidate satisfying the preregistered eligibility rules. (2) The selected question yields no substantiated finding or resolved uncertainty within the investigation budget. (3) A fresh successor session answers fewer than 4 of 5 handoff questions correctly under the frozen rubric. INTERPRETATION: (1) These criteria assess this bounded pilot, not Moltbook's general usefulness. (2) Service unavailability, inaccessible content or failed instrumentation is a blocker or unassessed result, not scientific falsification. (3) Independent evidence may contradict the originating post; a well-supported correction is a successful learning outcome. (4) An investigation that establishes only that evidence is insufficient must identify the specific evidential gap and a discriminating next test; a generic statement of uncertainty does not count as a resolved uncertainty. (5) No result establishes that Moltbook is better than other discovery sources because this pilot has no matched comparison arm.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-06T18:08:29.993245+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-058/assessment.md): Pilot disposition (not a verdict on Moltbook): discovery valid (3 eligible candidates from 20 posts) and investigation substantiated (corrected a post on Landauer/deletion/flash retention with independent sources and a reproducible computation), but the fresh successor scored 3 of 5 under the frozen rubric (threshold 4): two required-item omissions, no fabrication. Token ceiling exceeded (successor alone 46,496 measured).
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Write continuity rubrics as atomic checks and do not cap successor answers below what the rubric requires.
  * Check remaining token budget before launching the successor test and measure own usage.
  * Concrete, checkable claims on Moltbook were rare (3 of the 12 posts evaluated); one yielded a real correction with primary sources.

### MISSION-062: Is the Proof Regime for the Most Frequent Sumset Sizes Far From Sharp? An Exhaustive Check for 3-Element Sets (Rank #46)
- **Status**: `PROPOSED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: Additive combinatorics: sizes of h-fold sumsets of 3-element subsets of {1,...,q} (exhaustive counting by local deterministic computation; bounded CPU)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `claude`)
- **Fallback Models**: `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > For k = 3 and every h in {5,...,16}, at every q in [3h, 250] the h most frequent values of |hA| over the 3-element subsets A of {1,...,q} are exactly P_0,...,P_(h-1), where P_l = C(h+2,2) - C(l+1,2), each occurring for strictly more sets than every other size. Equivalently, the empirical threshold q0(h,3) is at most 3h in this range, far below the h^5 scaling that the proof of Corollary 4.1 in arXiv:2611.07303 requires.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > FALSIFIED if any (h,q) with h in {5,...,16} and 3h <= q <= 250 fails the ok-test (some P_l has f_q(P_l) = 0 or f_q(P_l) <= the maximum f_q over all unlisted sizes; a tie counts as failure), after the failing cell is recomputed by the independent reference implementation. UNASSESSED, neither corroborated nor falsified, if the validity gate fails (reproduce the paper's published threshold cells (h,k) = (3,3)->5, (4,3)->6, (2,4)->8, (3,4)->16 with failures at q = 4, 5, 7, 15; exact agreement between the fast and the reference implementation for every h <= 6, q <= 40; |hE| = 2h+1 for E = {1,2,3}, h >= 2) or if the budget is exhausted before the whole region is covered. The constant 3, the h range, the q bound 250, the ok-test and the budget are fixed in protocol.md and committed before the held-out run and are not changed afterwards. Results for h <= 4 and the k = 4 cells are calibration, not primary evidence; secondary tables cannot rescue a failed primary claim. No claim is made for q > 250, h > 16, k != 3, or asymptotic truth, and a corroboration is evidence about a finite range, not a proof. The cited paper's claims are context, not evidence for this hypothesis.

### MISSION-065: Is the Golden Angle the Finite-N Optimum of a Sunflower (Vogel) Spiral? (Rank #47)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: Phyllotaxis geometry: minimum pairwise distance of Vogel spirals r=sqrt(k), theta=2*pi*k*t for N in {100,200,400,800} (Python standard library; bounded local CPU)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `local-cpu` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `none`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Let d_min(t,N) be the minimum pairwise distance of the Vogel spiral with N points and divergence t (fraction of a turn), t_g = 2 - phi. On held-out N in {100,200,400,800}: (H1) some t within +/-1 deg of t_g achieves d_min >= 1.01 x d_min(t_g,N) at every N (golden is measurably beatable); (H2) the window-best angle lies within 0.1 deg of t_g at every N (but only by a near neighbour); (H3) for N in {100,200}, the best t over the full range [0.02,0.5] lies inside the +/-1 deg golden window. (G) Validity gate: grid-hash d_min equals brute force within 1e-12 on all checked configurations, and the analytic t=1/2 case matches sqrt(N)-sqrt(N-2).
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > FALSIFIED if gate G passes and any of H1, H2 or H3 fails on the held-out N. UNASSESSED if G fails or the held-out run does not finish. Dev N in {25,50} only for instrument checks; protocol.md, evaluate_vogel.py and freeze.json are hash-frozen and committed before held-out execution. Scan resolution is fixed at step 0.05/(2*pi*N^1.5) plus 3 rounds of x10 local refinement; it is a grid search, so 'best' means best found, a lower bound on the true supremum.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-08T17:16:06.304950+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-065/README.md): Gate passed (grid==brute 1e-12, analytic t=1/2). H1 failed: best nearby angle beats golden d_min by only 0.24%/0.05%/0.04%/0.04% at N=100/200/400/800 (<1%). H2 held (offsets +0.074..+0.012 deg). H3 held (full-range best inside golden window at N=100,200). Frozen 3044ab5a8; 111.3s CPU.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * On the min-distance metric the golden angle is within 0.04-0.24% of the best angle found at N=100..800; the residual is set by the inner core (seeds 1 and 4), not the bulk.
  * Finite-N optimal divergence angles sit slightly above golden (+0.012 deg at N=400,800) and shift the bottleneck pair outward (seeds 208,242).

- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `local-cpu` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `none`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Let E(N) be the worst error in cents, over the just intervals 3/2, 5/4 and 6/5, when each interval is rounded independently to the nearest step of N-tone equal temperament. N is a record if E(N) < E(M) for every M < N. Held-out range N in 31..200: (H1) both 53 and 118 are records; (H2) every record in 31..200 is in {31, 34, 53, 65, 87, 118, 171}. (G) Validity gate: for N=12 the errors are 1.955, 13.686 and 15.641 cents (within 0.001), and the vectorised record scan matches a brute pairwise check on N in 1..30.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > FALSIFIED if gate G passes and H1 or H2 fails on N in 31..200. CORROBORATED if G passes and both hold. UNASSESSED if G fails. Dev range N in 1..30 is used only for instrument checks; protocol.md, evaluate_et.py and freeze.json are hash-frozen and committed before the held-out run.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-08T18:14:16.784857+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-066/README.md): Gate passed (N=12 errors match; scan==brute on 1..30). Records in 31..200: 31,34,53,118,171. H1 held (53,118 records); H2 held (all in allowed set; 65,87 absent). Frozen 8041b5b8b; <1s CPU.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Under worst-case patent-rounded 5-limit error, the record ETs to 200 are 1,2,3,5,7,12,19,31,34,53,118,171: tuning lore holds, and no division in 54..117 beats 53.
  * 12-TET's 5-limit weakness is its thirds (14-16 cents), not its fifth (2 cents).

### MISSION-067: Random Change Ringing as a Shuffle: Does Ringing's One-Place Rule Mix Bells Fast When Swaps Run in Parallel? (Rank #53)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `local`
- **Target Platform**: Exact Markov chain distribution evolution on the symmetric group S_n, n in 4..8 (Python standard library; bounded local CPU)
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `local-cpu` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `none`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `qwen2-7b-mlx-4bit`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Chain C (random change): from rounds (identity), each step applies a uniformly random nonempty set of disjoint adjacent transpositions on n bells. Chain A (baseline): lazy random adjacent transposition (stay with prob 1/2, else swap a uniform adjacent pair). t_X(n) = least t with total variation distance to uniform on S_n <= 0.25. Held-out n in {7,8}: (H1) speedup R(n) = t_A(n)/t_C(n) is larger than R(6) for both n=7 and n=8, and R(8) > R(7); (H2) total expected swaps to mix, t_C(n)*s_C(n), is below t_A(n)*0.5 at both n=7 and n=8, where s_C(n) is the mean swaps per change (parallelism saves work, not just time). (G) Gate: exact evolution conserves probability within 1e-9; the number of nonempty changes equals F(n+1)-1 (Fibonacci); TV is non-increasing in t for chain A; dev n in {4,5,6}.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > FALSIFIED if gate G passes and H1 or H2 fails at held-out n. CORROBORATED if G passes and both hold. UNASSESSED if G fails or the held-out run does not finish within budget (t cap 5000 steps, 20 min CPU). Dev n in {4,5,6} only; protocol.md, evaluate_ringing.py and freeze.json are hash-frozen and committed before the held-out run.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-08T18:35:35.531421+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-067/README.md): Gate passed (Fibonacci move count, mass conserved, A monotone). Held-out: R=t_A/t_C = 2.88/3.54/3.97 at n=6/7/8 (H1 held). Swaps C/A = 1.07 (n=7), 1.08 (n=8) > 1 (H2 failed). Frozen abda842f3; 5.3 s CPU.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Random ringing changes (parallel disjoint adjacent swaps) mix S_n 3.5-4x faster in steps than lazy adjacent transposition at n=7,8, but use 7-8% more total swaps: parallelism buys time, not work.
  * Swap overhead fell from 1.16 at n=6 to about 1.07 at n=7,8; whether it tends to 1 is open.

### MISSION-035: Measured Agent Usage Telemetry: Orchestrator-Queried Before/After Token and Quota Snapshots per Mission, Feeding Evidence-Based Model Assignment (Rank #60)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `FALSIFIED`
- **Execution Surface**: `hybrid`
- **Target Platform**: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (agy) CLIs and the local MLX server (Copilot only under an explicit human-approved, usage-query-only exception); the evaluating-agent-work skill; the cli-agent skill
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-haiku-5.5` (Tier: `cheap`, CLI: `cli-agent`)
- **Fallback Models**: `gemini-3.8-flash`, `codex`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > A deterministic usage probe run by the orchestrator (not self-reported by the worker model) that snapshots each backend's own usage surfaces at every real mission checkout and checkin, and stores the measured delta with task class, model, wall-clock time, turns, retries and outcome quality in the evaluating-agent-work ledger, yields: (a) measurable per-task token deltas for >= 3 of the 4 backends (claude, codex, agy, local) agreeing within +/-10% with the vendor's own session totals; (b) where a backend exposes quota-window state (5-hour and weekly), a before/after window reading flagged noisy whenever other sessions were active; (c) after >= 12 real measured tasks, a per-task-class predictor whose held-out MAPE on tokens is <= 30% and >= 20% lower than the static per-task ceilings in track_budget.py; (d) a measured effort multiplier per (backend/model, task class): cost, wall-clock time and retry rate relative to a reference model, so that 'cheap per credit' models are not recommended on price alone when they cost several times the time and effort on a task class; and (e) a model-assignment recommendation that weighs expected cost, time, success rate and remaining 5-hour/weekly headroom, and shifts load to a backend with headroom when another is constrained, with zero credentials, auth tokens or prompt contents written to any tracked file. (f) A fuel gauge visible at boot and at checkout flags any backend whose tightest window is under 15% remaining, and a calibrated percent-to-token estimate predicts the next window percent movement within +/-50% once >= 5 non-concurrent percent points of data exist.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > Fewer than 3 backends yield a measurable per-task delta; any delta deviates > 10% from the vendor-reported session total; the held-out MAPE is > 30% or not >= 20% better than the static estimates; a quota-window reading cannot be attributed (other sessions' usage swamps the mission's own delta) and no mitigation restores attribution; any auth token, API key or prompt text appears in a tracked file or log; the probe reaches Copilot (a corporate account the cli-agent skill marks work-only) without explicit per-run human approval and usage-query-only scope; or obtaining a backend's quota state requires scraping an undocumented private endpoint or violating its terms (then record that backend as unmeasurable, not hacked). If worker self-report proves as accurate as orchestrator measurement, the measured path is not justified and the result is recorded as such. Also falsified if, with >= 12 real tasks, the measured data shows no usable difference in effective cost or time between models within a task class (the effort multiplier is noise), or the recommender's top choice is outperformed on effective cost by a random choice among unconstrained backends on held-out tasks. Also falsified if the calibrated percent-to-token estimate misses subsequent percent movement by more than 50% on >= 3 held-out measurements, or if a backend reaches 0% remaining without the gauge having flagged it LOW beforehand.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-05T05:42:18.438430+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-035/results-n14.md): N=14 measured tasks (11 claude, 1 codex, 2 agy). (c) per-class token predictor: held-out MAPE 122.3% vs static 166.2% (limit 30%; relative improvement 26.4% passes the 20% leg). (f) percent-to-token calibration 56,349 tokens/pct; leave-one-out 5 of 8 within +/-50%, 3 misses = the falsification threshold (misses are 1-2 pct tasks where integer rounding alone is 25-50%). (a) met for 3 of 4 backends with exact tokens; (b) partly met; (d) and (e) not testable at this N. Survived: exact tokens, catalog-based cost, fuel gauge, delegation recorder.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Free-text task classes are too fine for 14 tasks: use a few size buckets.
  * The claude window percent is an integer: calibrate on tasks that move it by >= 3 points or pool them.
  * A same-backend delegate shares the account window with its orchestrator: its window delta is unattributable.
  * Reasoning tokens bill as output: a cheap model's output count can be 8x its visible answer.

### MISSION-052: Four-Worker Parallel Batch With the Existing Stack: Two Codex, Antigravity and Local Qwen Under One Main-Thread Orchestrator, Without a New Orchestrator Skill (Rank #66)
- **Status**: `RESOLVED`
- **Empirical Verdict**: `CORROBORATED`
- **Execution Surface**: `hybrid`
- **Target Platform**: Claude Code orchestrator; Codex CLI x2, Antigravity CLI, local MLX Qwen2.5-Coder-7B; flight board, merge_prep, cli-agent, usage_hook
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-sonnet-5.5` (Tier: `standard`, CLI: `claude`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > A single main-thread orchestrator (Claude) using only the existing stack (flight board, manage_coordination, cli-agent, merge_prep, usage_hook delegated, validate_missions) can run ONE bounded batch of four concurrent workers (Codex A, Codex B, Antigravity, local Qwen2.5-Coder-7B), each in its own leased worktree, such that: (a) the four runs overlap for at least 50% of the shortest worker's runtime; (b) there are 0 undeclared edits outside leased paths and 0 writes into a peer worktree; (c) at least 3 of 4 deliveries are accepted after cross-vendor review and the orchestrator's own re-run of the acceptance checks; (d) measured tokens are attributable per worker session for at least 3 of 4 workers; (e) accepted deliveries integrate onto a dedicated integration branch with at most 1 conflict round each after merge_prep regeneration and a green combined suite; and (f) review finds at least 1 real defect the author's self-assessment missed.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > Any of: an undeclared edit, clobbered file or write into a peer worktree; fewer than 2 accepted deliveries; the workers were not concurrent (overlap under 50% of the shortest runtime); per-worker tokens attributable for fewer than 3 workers; an integration needing more than 1 conflict round despite merge_prep, or a red combined suite; a push, merge to main or publication without explicit human approval; the human-managed MLX server stopped or reconfigured; or review finds no defect in any of the four deliveries. This is NOT a test of MISSION-033's three-worker thresholds (60% wall-clock, 25% orchestrator overhead, 80% review agreement), and no speedup claim is valid without a measured baseline.
- **Empirical Evidence & Trials**:
  * `2026-11-06T07:20:00.738704+00:00` [claude-code] (LEARNING/experiments/mission-052/closeout.md): Orchestration-mechanics hypothesis (a)-(f) met by the round-1 four-worker batch (PR #350): overlap 87 s = 74% of the shortest worker's 117 s; verify clean for all four leases; 3 of 4 deliveries accepted after cross-vendor review (strict independence from the orchestrator: 2 of 4); tokens attributable per session for 3 of 4 workers; 4 merges with 0 conflicts, combined suite green (292 passed, 2 skipped); real defects found by review in the deliveries. Completion rounds (PRs #351, #355, #358) are corroborating context: 041 and 050 closed FALSIFIED, 004 inconclusive and open; merged changes stay within declared impact. Verdict is on the literal reading of clause (c) and the standing-authorization reading of the push/merge condition (quoted in closeout.md section 7); same-vendor review of the verdict (Codex out of quota). Not a test of MISSION-033 thresholds; no speedup claim; lease fencing (038) unimplemented. Recorded limitations: about 7 human corrections of avoidable failures, telemetry recorded zero; 480 Haiku calls launched before the experimental context was verified; the orchestrator's lock hold interrupted a worker; round 1 stopped at bounded slices until the human corrected the purpose; one batch, small N.
- **Lessons Learned & Epistemic Compounding**:
  * Define completion at the requested outcome level (verdicts), not at worker return.
  * Verify the experimental context with supported diagnostics before launching hundreds of calls.
  * A shared-resource hold by the orchestrator must be announced to the worker it affects.
  * Report telemetry gaps; hooks that write zero counters can misrepresent observed corrections.

### MISSION-053: Repair Demonstrated Causes of MISSION-052's Orchestration Failures in the Shared orchestrating-agent-work Skill (Guidance, References, Executor/Telemetry Checks), Verified by Executed Staged Scenarios (Rank #67)
- **Status**: `PROPOSED`
- **Execution Surface**: `hybrid`
- **Target Platform**: Companion repo richfrem/agent-plugins-skills (plugins/agent-orchestration/.apm/skills/orchestrating-agent-work); Claude Code orchestrator; Sanctuary Protocol 133 for source-then-install; APM global install
- **Cheapest Viable Model**: `claude-sonnet-5.5` (Tier: `standard`, CLI: `claude`)
- **Fallback Models**: `claude-haiku-5.5`, `gemini-3.8-flash`
- **Hypothesis (Popperian Prediction)**:
  > Repairing the demonstrated causes of the orchestration failures observed in MISSION-052 changes what an orchestrator actually DOES in staged, executable scenarios. The repair targets each failure's confirmed cause, which may be missing or ambiguous guidance, existing guidance that is hard to find or enforce, an executor or installation defect, or a telemetry defect; it is not assumed that more instructions are the fix, and it adds no new scheduler, ledger or control plane. Behavior is measured on ten scenario families by observable tool actions and state transitions recorded by a deterministic harness (never by what the model says it would do, and never by text matching against the skill): F1 partial deliverable returned while the assigned outcome is unfinished; F2 independent review started while another worker is still running; F3 cloud arm independent of a congested local resource started without waiting; F4 duplicate execution PREVENTED before launch when an execution unit is already owned (a duplicate that is only detected afterward counts as a failure); F5 progress reported from unique work units and verified artifacts when logs contain duplicate ids and malformed responses; F6 a required executable is verified inside the worker environment before dispatch; F7 prior authorization within scope is honored without a repeated permission question; F8 shared-resource contention is scheduled explicitly and its effect on experimental validity assessed; F9 misleading telemetry (zero friction or error counters despite observed failures and human corrections) is reported as a telemetry gap; F10 experimental-context preflight: before launching hundreds of experimental calls the orchestrator verifies, through supported diagnostics and not model self-report, what context the calls will actually carry (hooks, memory, instruction files, plugins, tools, working directory, session reuse), refuses or corrects a contaminated invocation, and records what remains unobservable (source: MISSION-052's 480-call Haiku arm ran with ambient hooks, memory and CLAUDE.md loaded and its hook wrote zero-valued telemetry into the experiment folder). Development and evaluation are separated: each family has development variants used to shape the revision and frozen, unseen evaluation variants used only to judge it; the baseline (currently installed version) and the revised version run with the same model and configuration, in isolated sessions, with counterbalanced run order, with repeated runs per variant.
- **Falsification Gate**:
  > Preregistered, baseline-aware decision rule (written and frozen before either version is run): let p0 and p1 be the pooled pass rates over all frozen evaluation cases (pass = every deterministic assertion for the case holds) for the baseline and the revised version. (1) If p0 >= 0.90 the benchmark cannot demonstrate improvement: report that, and investigate whether the scenarios actually reproduce the observed execution failures (for example by replaying the recorded MISSION-052 decision points) instead of weakening the target. (2) Otherwise the required gain is g = min(0.20, 0.95 - p0). CORROBORATED only if p1 >= 0.80 AND p1 - p0 >= g AND the paired bootstrap 95% interval for p1 - p0 excludes zero AND no family is worse than baseline by more than 0.20. (3) FALSIFIED if p1 < 0.80 or p1 - p0 < g or the interval includes zero or any family regresses by more than 0.20. Per-family results and run-to-run variability are reported; no wording is tuned against evaluation variants. Not falsification, but acceptance requirements that block integration: the skill's existing tests and evals still pass; the main SKILL.md stays concise (growth beyond roughly 25% needs a stated reason); packaging and link checks pass; unnecessary duplication of existing rules is judged explicitly in review. A packaging or link check passing is not evidence that behavior improved. Whether future orchestrators need fewer human corrections is longitudinal and not claimed.
